breaking_changes.BC_description: Dropped support for Node.js versions <18.19.0 and 20.0.0 - 20.4.0. Projects running on those Node.js versions will no longer work with this library version.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Upgrade your Node.js installation to >=18.19.0 or >=20.5.0 before using this version of the library.

breaking_changes.BC_description: When the 'encoding' option is set to 'buffer' in execa, the output (result.stdout, result.stderr, result.all) is now an Uint8Array instead of a Buffer.
Renamed allowed values for the 'encoding' option: null→'buffer', 'utf-8'/'UTF8'→'utf8', 'utf-16le'/ 'ucs2'/'ucs-2'→'utf16le', 'binary'→'latin1'.

Passing a file path or writable stream directly to subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), or subprocess.pipeAll() has been removed. Now, pass a {file: './path'} object or an array with ['pipe', stream] to the stdout or stderr options.

The subprocess.pipeStdout(), subprocess.pipeStderr(), and subprocess.pipeAll() methods have been renamed to subprocess.pipe(). Requires updating method usage and optionally specifying the 'from' piping option.
Renamed the 'signal' option to 'cancelSignal'. Update all usage to the new name for abort controller/cancellation handling.
Renamed error.killed to error.isTerminated. Downstream code should check isTerminated for termination status.
Removed subprocess.cancel(). Use subprocess.kill() or the cancelSignal option instead for terminating subprocesses.
Renamed forceKillAfterTimeout option to forceKillAfterDelay and changed location: pass it to execa() instead of subprocess.kill().
'verbose' option for execa is now a string enum: false→'none', true→'short'. Update usages accordingly.
Renamed execPath option to nodePath. Now, effective only if node: true. It also operates if preferLocal is false.
The default for the 'serialization' option is now 'advanced' instead of 'json'. Objects containing functions or symbols passed to subprocess.send() now throw instead of silently omitting.
Manual piping via subprocess.stdout.pipe, subprocess.stderr.pipe, or subprocess.all.pipe must now happen immediately after subprocess creation to capture early output.
Signals passed to subprocess.kill() or killSignal option can no longer be lowercase. Must use upper-case (e.g., 'SIGTERM').
